rationale: The workflow is a simple weekly scheduled job for sprint issue management that runs a Python check and GitHub Actions to move issues between sprints. It has no matrix, no dependency installation, no heavy computation, and no evidence of runaway execution. The retrieved patterns either do not apply (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST requires a matrix; P-LIT-GHA-CACHE requires repeated dependency fetching; P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE applies to push/PR triggers) or have contraindications: P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE is contraindicated because sprint updates are time-based and depend on external GitHub issue state, not just repository code changes; P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE is contraindicated because periodic sprint management is a mandatory project-management check; P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW shows only a 0.1% upper-bound reduction and requires an approved skip policy. No supported optimization meets its preconditions without violating contraindications or weakening required checks.
